study.title: Brain Network Response to Acupuncture Stimuli in Experimental Acute Low Back Pain: An fMRI Study
study.study_design: block design fMRI study; within-subject crossover; experimental acute low back pain (ALBP) model induced by hypertonic saline injection in healthy volunteers
study.randomization: pseudorandom order of ACUP and SHAM scans
study.blinding: subjects kept eyes and ears closed; subjects were purposely misguided that they would receive two different forms of acupuncture; single-blind (subjects blinded to condition type)
study.population: Twenty-eight healthy, right-handed subjects (11 women; age range: 22–30 years)
study.disease_condition: Experimental acute low back pain (ALBP) induced by intramuscular hypertonic saline injection
study.inclusion_criteria: healthy, right-handed; some knowledge of acupuncture due to previous cultural exposure; never received acupuncture treatment; body mass index within the standard range (±10%); no psychiatric or medical illnesses (i.e., multiple sclerosis and epilepsy); no painful episodes (including dysmenorrhea) or did not take any drugs (i.e., antipyretics and sleeping pills) within the last month
study.exclusion_criteria: psychiatric or medical illnesses (i.e., multiple sclerosis and epilepsy); painful episodes (including dysmenorrhea) or drugs (i.e., antipyretics and sleeping pills) within the last month; head movements more than 1.5 mm or 1.5° (motion exclusion during MRI preprocessing)

conditions.timepoint_exact: prior to ALBP induction; 6 min resting state scan
conditions.scan_context: resting state fMRI; eyes and ears covered; lying still

conditions.timepoint_exact: during first 6 min of ALBP stimulation (hypertonic saline injection ongoing)
conditions.scan_context: resting state fMRI during experimental ALBP; eyes and ears covered
conditions.dose_or_intensity_label: bolus injection 0.1 mL within 5 s then continuous injection 0.15 mL/min

conditions.timepoint_exact: during ON blocks of ACUP functional scan; ALBP occurring continually throughout
conditions.scan_context: task fMRI block design; six 30 s ON blocks interspersed with six 30 s OFF blocks; 6 min total scan

conditions.condition_label_exact: OFF status (rest blocks during ACUP scan)
conditions.timepoint_exact: during OFF blocks of ACUP functional scan
conditions.scan_context: task fMRI block design; six 30 s OFF blocks

conditions.timepoint_exact: during ON blocks of SHAM functional scan; ALBP occurring continually throughout
conditions.scan_context: task fMRI block design; six 30 s ON blocks interspersed with six 30 s OFF blocks; 6 min total scan
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Needle is vertically inserted to a depth of 1.5 cm (15 mm), which far exceeds the 5 mm threshold for full penetration. At this depth the needle reaches muscle/fascia and activates deep mechanoreceptors, placing this firmly at Level 1 regardless of the saline injection manipulation.

conditions.condition_label_exact: OFF status (rest blocks during SHAM scan)
conditions.timepoint_exact: during OFF blocks of SHAM functional scan
conditions.scan_context: task fMRI block design; six 30 s OFF blocks
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Same needle insertion depth of 1.5 cm (15 mm) applies during the OFF/rest blocks of the same sham scan session. The physical tissue engagement is identical to the ON blocks; only the task/injection timing differs. Full penetration to muscle/fascia depth qualifies as Level 1.

interventions.procedure_label_exact: ALBP model induced by hypertonic saline injection
non_acupoint_locations_exact: 2 cm lateral to the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: right lower back muscle; 2 cm lateral to the spinous process of the fourth lumbar vertebra
interventions.penetration_exact: vertically inserted at a depth of 1.5 cm
interventions.manipulation_exact: bolus injection (0.1 mL within 5 s) and subsequent continuous injection (0.15 mL/min); sterile hypertonic saline (10 mL, 5%); attached via a long connecting tube to a computer-controlled power injector (Spectris Solaris EP; Medrad, Inc., Warrendale, PA, USA)
interventions.session_duration_exact: 6 min pain status scan (injection ongoing continually throughout subsequent scans)
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: to induce a persistent moderate-high pain in ALBP subject

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: midpoint of the transverse crease of the popliteal fossa; right lower limb
interventions.needle_type_exact: nonmagnetic (pure silver), 0.4 mm-diameter, 60 mm-long acupuncture needle (Beijing Zhongyan Taihe Medicine Co., Ltd, Beijing, China)
interventions.manipulation_exact: manually twirled (±180°) at 1 Hz with 'even reinforcing and reducing' needle manipulation in traditional Chinese medicine
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; to obtain a subjective acupuncture sensation, namely, de qi sensation
interventions.needle_retention_exact: during six 30 s ON blocks of each functional scan (total 6 min scan)
interventions.session_duration_exact: 6 min functional scan (six 30 s ON blocks, six 30 s OFF blocks)
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: subjects asked to keep eyes and ears closed; subjects purposely misguided that they would receive two different forms of acupuncture and needed to concentrate on the degree of acupuncture sensations of BL40
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: BL40 (Weizhong acupoint) is considered as one of the four most important acupoints and proven to have unique efficacy in the treatment of ALBP

interventions.stimulation_type: tactile stimulation with von Frey monofilament
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: skin of the BL40; right lower limb
interventions.needle_type_exact: von Frey monofilament delivered through a needle-guide tube
interventions.penetration_exact: non-penetrating; tapped gently over the skin
interventions.manipulation_exact: acupuncturist poked the monofilament through a needle-guide tube and tapped it gently over the skin of the BL40 with the same amplitude and rate as that used during ACUP
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: no; designed to control for superficial and cutaneous somatosensory effects; subjects expected 'ACUP'
interventions.needle_retention_exact: during six 30 s ON blocks of each functional scan (total 6 min scan)
interventions.session_duration_exact: 6 min functional scan (six 30 s ON blocks, six 30 s OFF blocks)
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: subjects asked to keep eyes and ears closed; subjects purposely misguided that they would receive two different forms of acupuncture
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: SHAM aimed to control for not only the superficial and cutaneous somatosensory effects around BL40 but also the cognitive processing induced by the subject's expectation of 'ACUP'

extraction_notes.note: Table 3 (SHAM minus OFF status) lists 'Right dlPFC' with BA 46 and X coordinate -48, and 'Left dlPFC' with BA 8 and X coordinate 37. The laterality labeling based on X coordinate sign appears potentially inconsistent with hemisphere labels in Table 3 (e.g., Left dlPFC BA8 has positive X=37, Right dlPFC BA46 has negative X=-48). These have been extracted exactly as printed in the table.
Table 3 Row 'Left Hp' is labeled BA 23, which is posterior cingulate, not hippocampus. This has been extracted exactly as printed.

Table 2 (ACUP minus OFF status) lists 'Left dmPFC' with BA 24 and coordinates (15, 20, 20), which has a positive X coordinate. This is extracted exactly as printed despite potential laterality ambiguity.

Table 4 (ACUP minus SHAM) lists 'Left thalamus' with coordinates (12, 34, 0) — positive X — and 'Right thalamus' coordinates (24, -27, 4). The positive X for 'Left thalamus' is unusual; extracted exactly as printed.
Table 4 lists 'Left ACC' with BA not reported and Z=-45, which would place it very inferiorly (below thalamus). This is extracted exactly as printed and may reflect an OCR or printing error.

Numeric deqi subscale values (soreness, numbness, heaviness, fullness) for ACUP and SHAM are shown only in Figure 5 bar charts. The paper does not report these numeric values in text. Only the significant p-values are stated in the text.
Expectancy and credibility ratings were not formally assessed with validated instruments (e.g., CEQ). No expectancy or credibility data are reported.
Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the paper.
No trial registration number is provided.
The study has a single arm (all subjects received ALBP model plus both ACUP and SHAM in crossover fashion). Arm structure represents the within-subject conditions rather than separate parallel arms.

The 'n_total_randomized' cannot be confirmed; the paper states 28 subjects participated without explicitly stating they were randomized as a group. The order of ACUP and SHAM was pseudorandom within subjects.
Table 2, row 'Left PAG' has no BA listed (column shows empty/dash) but cluster size 44 is reported. Similarly 'Right HP' has no BA. These are extracted with 'not_reported' for BA.

The paper identifies this as the first fMRI study of acupuncture in experimental ALBP, and the ALBP group served as both baseline (no pain) and clinical (pain) comparator within subjects — there is no healthy control without pain or separate sham-only arm for between-group clinical comparison.

Table 3 row 'Right pACC' has BA 23 and coordinates (5, -50, 42), and 'Left ACC' has BA 24 and coordinates (-4, -66, 22). Negative Y values for ACC/pACC are atypical; these are extracted exactly as printed.
Table 4 title says 'fMRJ' (likely OCR/typographic error for 'fMRI'). Extracted as fMRI in the JSON.
Table 3 angular gyrus rows show BA 19 but with negative Z coordinates (-27 and -34), which is unusual for BA19. Extracted exactly as printed.

The cluster extent units (voxels) are inferred from context (SPM8, no cluster size unit explicitly labeled in table headers). The tables provide 'Cluster sizes' without specifying voxels vs mm3; voxels is standard for SPM8 output.
